messages:
maria: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak I see a p99 decode latency bump on a subset of traffic (RQ-6). Not huge, but reproducible in staging and correlates with KV cache miss spikes. Posting the minimal profile excerpt I grabbed.
ashwin: saw the alert this morning. can you paste the logs and the config you rolled?

maria: sure, paste below. note the bump is only on short decode-heavy calls (prefill fine).

```
2025-03-12T09:02:11Z p99_total_ms: 120 -> 185  # baseline -> after-change
2025-03-12T09:02:11Z p50_total_ms: 35 -> 38
2025-03-12T09:02:11Z kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.82 -> 0.61
2025-03-12T09:02:11Z avg_batch_size_prefill: 8.1 -> 8.0
2025-03-12T09:02:11Z avg_batch_size_decode: 1.3 -> 1.2
2025-03-12T09:02:11Z decode_queue_wait_ms: +40
```

maria: config delta (snip):
```
kernel_selector: v2
phase_routing: enabled
batching: continuous
token_budget_target: 48  # previously 64 for decode lanes
kv_priming_window_ms: 25 -> 10
```

noah: interesting — token_budget_target smaller for decode could explain more decode queue churn and more KV cold misses if we hand off kernels more often. also kernel v2 has slightly different batch alignment that favors prefill.

kevin: +1. we saw KV thrash in a different change where decode microbatches were being forcibly split; the demux/handshake frequency matters a lot. can you run a quick ablation with token_budget_target=96 for decode?

ashwin: I'd rather we try separating prefill vs decode batching policies completely for this canary. keep kernel_selector v2 but set decode.token_budget_target=96 and decode.max_microbatch_ms=200, prefill keep token_budget_target=48. see if decode latency stabilizes without losing prefill efficiency.

maria: launching a staging canary with those overrides now. will pin to a small cohort (10% gen-only). deploybot: canary request (env=staging, cohort=gen-only-10%) queued.

deploybot: canary deployed: rollout id r-20250312-59. Starting 10% traffic to staging cluster s-crux-07.

maria: early metrics after 10m: p99 decode back to ~130ms, kv_hit_rate 0.78, decode_queue_wait down 18ms. looks promising.

noah: nice. can you also capture kernel handoff frequency? we want to know whether handoffs dropped (less churn) or if priming window increase just hid it.

maria: grabbed a quick counter:
```
handoff_count_per_min: before 820/min -> after 420/min (on cohort)
kv_evictions_per_min: before 190/min -> after 105/min
```

kevin: that handoff reduction is the smoking gun. fewer handoffs -> less KV thrash -> better decode p99. But we need to test cost: larger token_budget for decode can increase tail latency for big gens if they block kernel for longer. have we seen any throughput regressions?

maria: throughput stable on cohort; end-to-end token/sec slightly up due to fewer retries. per-route cost delta is negligible in the 10m window.

lina: takeaways: (1) kernel_selector v2 is fine but pairing it with too-small decode token_budget causes handshake churn, (2) KV priming window reduction made it worse, (3) separating decode vs prefill batching heuristics (explicit lane configs) recovers p99.

lina: plan: roll separation config to broader canary (30%) for 1h, run kbench and long-running regen tests, instrument kernel_handoff_count and kv_eviction histograms. if stable, codify lane-aware defaults and add an opt-in "entropy gating" flag for aggressive priming for prefill-only lanes.

noah: +1. also add a small experiment: try adaptive token_budget_target that expands on repeated handoffs (e.g., multiplier 1.5 after 2 handoffs in 500ms). might be lower-risk than just bumping static budgets.

ashwin: agree — adaptive looks promising. but for short-term mitigation, let's promote the explicit lane separation change and revert the kv_priming_window shrink.

maria: will push PR with config + metrics dashboard links. PR will include a runbook for rollback.

lina: thanks all. tagging @kevin to review the canary perf logs, @noah to prototype adaptive heuristic, and @ashwin to own rollout gate. :thumbsup:

kevin: reviewing now, will post comments on the PR.

deploybot: canary r-20250312-59: expanded to 30% at 2025-03-12T10:18:40Z per request.

maria: updated last: 30% run looks stable at 45m mark. leaving canary running for the 1h window before TL;DR postmortem.

lina: closing loop later with postmortem notes and a short ops doc on lane separation.
